newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian police, protesters clash on Belgrade streets.
newsitem.headline: Serbian police, protesters clash on Belgrade streets.

text.p: Police and opposition supporters fought running street battles in the centre of the Serbian capital overnight, with anti-riot squads using water cannon and baton charges to clear streets.
Demonstrators, seeking the reinstatement of local election victories by the opposition last November, fought back with stones and bottles and built makeshift barricades of burning tyres.

The trouble began after anti-riot police refused to allow a relatively small contingent of several hundred opposition supporters to cross a river bridge to the city centre for a 77th straight day of pro-democracy protests.
Larger groups of protesters, hearing the news, turned away from their usual destination in Republic Square and blocked both sides of the bridge in a stand-off lasting about three hours.

After the bridge was forcibly cleared, protesters and police clashed in the city's old quarter. Water cannon doused protesters, who threw stones, bricks and bottles as burning tyres lit up the night sky in a lurid red.

Witnesses saw several people with blood pouring down their faces after more police charges. They also said they experienced a burning sensation in their noses and mouths suggesting that teargas was being used.
